figures.caption: Figure 1. Motivation and overview of SENSA. (a) Complementary visual cues motivate structured response modeling; component-to-response arrows are schematic. (b) A training-mean ERP can match shared activity without image specificity. (c) Fullresponse synthesis motivates evaluating image-dependent prediction separately. (d) SENSA calibrates a frozen shared generator through Factor Transport and Residual Memory.

Figure 2. SENSA architecture for sensor-time responses. (a) Visual coefficients weight shared response bases; the Response Refiner yields the population prediction. (b) FT adapts channel mixing, timing, and factor amplitudes. (c) RM maps image keys to error coordinates through coordinate-wise PRESS-selected Ridge, including zero correction. The target support mean ps is added separately. Waveforms and transformations are schematic.

Figure 6. Source-grounded memory and downstream utility. EEG: 10 subjects, seed 42, K400, all 200 test images. (a) Coordinates. (b) Global versus coordinate-wise Ridge. (c) RM-key mismatch, FT fixed; three permutations/subject. (d) Real-EEG decoding with/without augmentation; three decoder seeds/subject. Diamonds/bars/bold: means; circles/lines: subjects; whiskers/band: 95% subject-bootstrap intervals. Protocols: Secs. O.1 and S.
